questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Look over your shoulder toward the direction you want to go.
Use only your left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder toward the direction you want to go.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Check multiple times before moving. Watch traffic in front of you and beside you.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see blind spots by looking in your rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have large blind spots. Other drivers should stay away from these areas.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: This sign appears on slow-moving vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings warn drivers about hazards. Round signs warn only about railroad crossings.

questions.question: When approaching a flashing red traffic signal, you must:

options.text: Stop completely, let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass, then proceed.
Slow down and continue with caution.
Stop and stay stopped until the light turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass, then proceed.
questions.explanation: A flashing red signal works like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop. Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Go when it is safe.

questions.question: When driving near a large truck, you should:

options.text: Stay close behind it to reduce wind resistance on your car.
Avoid staying beside it for long periods.
Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid staying beside it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots on both sides. Do not stay beside them for long periods.

questions.question: When can you legally block an intersection?

options.text: If the traffic light is green when you enter it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can cross completely before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: What does alcohol affect first?
questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms all abilities needed for safe driving. It travels from your stomach to your blood to your entire body. Alcohol damages the brain areas that control judgment and skill.

questions.question: Alcohol in any amount is:
questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is always a depressant. It slows all nerve signals and body functions. It reduces self-control and harms concentration and alertness.

questions.question: After holding your license for six months, which passenger cannot be in your car while you drive?
questions.correctAnswerText: Your 18-year-old friend.
questions.explanation: During the first six months, you can only have a driving instructor, parents or guardians, or someone at least 20 years old as passengers. After six months, you can also have immediate family members.

questions.question: What does a blood alcohol concentration of 0.02 percent do?

options.text: It has no effect on your driving.
It does not put other drivers at risk.
It doubles your chance of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: It doubles your chance of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Each 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol concentration nearly doubles a driver's risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass if you are in the lane next to the solid yellow line.
You cannot pass from either direction.
You can pass if you are in the lane next to the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass if you are in the lane next to the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means drivers in the lane with the broken line can pass. Drivers in the lane with the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: What must you do when a school bus ahead on your side has its red lights flashing?

options.text: Slow down to no more than 10 mph.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights, you must stop. Do not move until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled in. Never pass a school bus that is picking up or dropping off students.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in bad weather or low light?
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, or rain. High beam headlights reflect back and create glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, you must yield to any driver who:
questions.correctAnswerText: Arrived before you.
questions.explanation: Vehicles should go through a four-way stop in the order they arrived. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the one on the left must yield to the one on the right.

questions.question: When pulling into traffic from a parked position, you should:

options.text: Drive slower than other traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a large gap so you can reach the same speed as other traffic.
Wait for two vehicles to pass, then drive into the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a large gap so you can reach the same speed as other traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic, wait for a gap large enough to match the speed of other vehicles.

questions.question: If you drive slower than other traffic, you will most likely:

options.text: Block traffic and get a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block traffic and get a ticket.
questions.explanation: Drive slower in heavy traffic or bad weather. But if you drive too slowly and block traffic flow, you may get a ticket. Match the speed of traffic, unless traffic exceeds the speed limit.

questions.question: When a red light shows a green arrow, you may go if you:

options.text: Come to a complete stop first.
Are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You can go in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the correct lane. First, yield to pedestrians and any vehicles already in the intersection.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the center mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line means no passing. If one line is solid and one is broken, only the driver in the lane with the broken line can pass. If both lines are solid, no one can pass from either direction.

questions.question: Before stopping at a traffic light or sign, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors for other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for other traffic.
questions.explanation: When stopping, check your mirrors first. Be aware of surrounding traffic. Release the accelerator to slow down. Then press the brake pedal smoothly for a controlled stop.

questions.question: Your car breaks down on the highway. What should you do?

options.text: Move all four wheels off the road if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move all four wheels off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: When your car breaks down, move it completely off the main road if you can. Keep all four wheels away from traffic.

questions.question: After drinking several beers, how can you reduce alcohol's effects?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wait several hours.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not speed this up. Your body needs about one hour to process one drink.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you on a city street. What should you do?

options.text: Drive to the right edge and slow down.
Drive to the right edge and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge and stop.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass. Move to the right edge of the road and stop until the vehicle passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through first, then stop.

questions.question: You stopped for a train at a railroad crossing. After the train passes, what should you do?

options.text: Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Watch for a second train after the first one passes. Do not drive until all gates are up and all warning lights have stopped flashing.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show all areas around your car. You must look over your shoulder to see blind spots before changing lanes.
